title: Async span stitcher and canonical header normalizer for mixed-sync runtimes
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Across Redwood services we observe fragmented trace graphs for requests that cross sync code, async worker queues, and HTTP->queue->worker paths. Multiple headers (traceparent, b3, custom X-RWD-Trace) arrive inconsistent or duplicated, causing duplicated root spans and noisy topology in the console. Goal: implement a lightweight "stitcher" component paired with a canonical header normalizer to reliably re-associate partial spans from async workers to their originating request and provide a single canonical carrier format for internal services and SDKs.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical header normalizer accepts traceparent, b3 (single and multi-header), and X-RWD-Trace and emits x-rwd-ctx with compact 64/128-bit ids
Async stitcher re-links worker-produced spans to originating request in 99.9% of test scenarios (synthetic fan-in, delayed processing up to 10s, duplicate headers)
SDK shim exposes a zero-copy attach/detach API for async boundaries with <2us median overhead per attach in microbenchmark
End-to-end traces in staging show no duplicate roots for queue-based flows and flamegraphs remain readable with correct parent-child relationships
Rollout plan exists with canary, metric alerts, and automatic fallback to legacy propagation if >0.5% increase in trace loss is detected
notes: Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Async+Span+Stitcher+Design (internal) — initial draft covers matching heuristic and tombstone TTL
Benchmarks: local synthetic harness (attached to PR) shows stitch success at 10k req/s with 2ms average matching latency
We introduce a compact canonical header x-rwd-ctx carrying: trace_id, parent_id, flags, and a lineage nonce for idempotency
Stitcher strategy: prefer explicit lineage nonce -> fallback to (trace_id + sampled bit + source-service) -> finally tolerate best-effort matches with confidence score
Tombstone policy: keep recent mapping for 60s in local in-memory LRU; downstream persistence via Redis cluster if cross-instance matching required (opt-in via config)
Compatibility: ensure incoming legacy b3 multi-header and traceparent are both recognized and normalized; outgoing traffic from Redwood services uses x-rwd-ctx by default behind SDK feature flag
progress_updates: 2026-02-22: Kickoff sync with SDK, runtime and infra teams. Agreed canonical header schema and basic API shape for shims.
2026-02-28: Prototype normalizer implemented in gateway proxy (Go) and tested against b3/traceparent corpus — parsing success 100% for sampled traces.
2026-03-04: SDK shim API reviewed; Node and Python wrappers accepted. Node shim uses async_hooks fallback when available, Python uses contextvars + queue token attach.
2026-03-09: Integration test harness added to staging: HTTP->SQS->worker flow with deliberate header duplication and delayed worker start. Stitcher re-associated 998/1000 traces in run.
2026-03-12: Performance microbench: attach/detach median 1.6us (Node), 2.1us (Python). Open PR for gateway normalizer and SDK shims: PR #7843
review_feedback: PM (Rafael Gomes): add schema versioning to x-rwd-ctx header to allow future extension without breaking older consumers
Security (Maya Ortiz): ensure canonical header doesn't leak PII; lineage nonce must be random and rotate per-request — proposed 128-bit random
Infra (Omar K): prefer in-memory tombstone + optional Redis for cross-instance; add circuit-breaker when Redis latency high to avoid request-path amplification
Observability (Priya Singh): add metrics: stitch_success_rate, stitch_latency_ms_p50/p95/p99, canonicalizer_parse_errors, header_normalizer_rewrites
next_steps: Merge gateway normalizer PR after addressing schema-version header (ETA 2026-03-15)
Publish Node/Python SDK shims behind feature flag and run 1-week canary on low-traffic services
Add Redis-backed tombstone as opt-in config and run failure-injection tests to validate circuit-breaker behavior
Create console rollout toggle and alerts: alert when stitch_success_rate < 99.5% for 10m
Post-mortem template ready in case of trace regressions; assign on-call owner for first 48h after rollout
external_notes: We will communicate changes to partners consuming raw headers — a migration doc will be published in the next 2 weeks.
No expected billing impact; telemetry event sizes unchanged (we carry canonical header in HTTP metadata only)
